instagram: Did you know motor oil doesn't just lubricate — it also cools, cleans, and protects your engine from corrosion? Over time it breaks down and stops doing all four jobs well. That's why interval matters more than mileage alone. 📚 #AutoTips #OilChangeFacts #CarCare101

Most brake pad wear isn't even visible from outside the wheel. By the time you hear squealing, you may have less than 2mm of pad left — that's under 1/8 inch between you and the rotor. A visual inspection takes 5 minutes and tells you exactly where you stand. 🔍 #BrakeSafety #AutoEducation

Tire pressure drops about 1 PSI for every 10°F temperature drop. That means your tires can lose 5-6 PSI in a single cold snap — affecting handling, braking, and fuel economy. Pro tip: check pressure in the morning before driving. 🌡️ #TireSafety #TirePressure #CarTips

Your cabin air filter cleans the air you breathe inside your car. A clogged one reduces AC/heat efficiency AND blows allergens and dust through your vents. Most drivers forget it exists — most manufacturers recommend replacing it every 12-15K miles. 💨 #CabinAirFilter #AirQuality #AutoMaintenance

Coolant doesn't just prevent freezing — it also raises the boiling point of your cooling system and prevents corrosion inside the engine. Old coolant becomes acidic and actually starts eating your radiator from the inside. Flush intervals vary by vehicle — ask us what yours needs. 🌡️ #CoolantFlush #EngineCare #AutoFacts
facebook: Quick auto education: your vehicle's owner manual lists two maintenance schedules — 'normal' and 'severe.' Most drivers qualify as 'severe' (frequent short trips, stop-and-go traffic, extreme temps, dusty roads). That means tighter oil change intervals than the sticker on your windshield suggests. Not sure which schedule you're on? Stop by [Shop Name] and we'll help you figure it out. [Phone]

Here's something most drivers don't know: wheel alignment and tire balance are two different services. Alignment adjusts the angle of your wheels relative to each other and the road. Balance corrects weight distribution within the tire/wheel assembly. Both affect tire wear and handling — but in different ways. If you're experiencing vibration, it's usually balance. If you're experiencing pulling or uneven wear, it's usually alignment. [Shop Name] — [Phone] — we'll diagnose it properly.

The check engine light covers over 200 different fault codes — from a loose gas cap to a misfiring cylinder. Ignoring it because the car 'seems fine' is one of the most common (and costly) mistakes we see. Some codes are minor. Some are early warnings of a major failure. The only way to know is a scan — which takes about 10 minutes. [Shop Name] offers free diagnostic scans. Call [Phone] or stop by.

Why do brake rotors warp? Heat. Every time you brake, friction generates heat. When hot rotors hit cold water (rain, puddles), they can warp slightly — creating that pulsing or vibrating feel when you stop. Avoiding heavy braking right before hitting water helps, but worn pads that create extra heat are the real culprit. If you feel pulsation, have your brakes inspected. [Shop Name] — [Phone].

Transmission fluid is often called 'lifetime fluid' by manufacturers — but that lifetime can be shorter than you think under real driving conditions. Heat, towing, and stop-and-go traffic degrade it faster. Dark brown or burned-smelling fluid is a red flag. Most independent shops (including us) recommend a service every 40-60K miles for most vehicles. Your transmission will thank you. [Shop Name] — [Phone].
